AUTODOC reports encouraging first-half results Online retailer for vehicle spare parts and accessories is undergoing organisational rightsizing to adapt to new challenges from a changing environment Sales revenue rose by 12.8% to €1,003.4 million between January and June Adjusted EBITDA increased by 13.7% to €91.9 million AUTODOC specifies and confirms outlook for 2026 CEO Dmitri Zadorojnii: „We are reorganising AUTODOC to remain capable of acting effectively even under more challenging conditions.“ Berlin, 13 August 2026 – Autodoc SE, the leading online retailer for vehicle spare parts and accessories in Europe, increased sales revenue and adjusted EBITDA by double-digit rates in the first half of 2026. „In a demanding environment, good financial results cannot be taken for granted. They are the product of hard work, necessary reorganisations and targeted efficiency measures. Past performance is no guarantee of future success, and given ongoing macroeconomic pressures and the need to capitalise on AI opportunities, maintaining strict cost discipline remains imperative”, says CEO Dmitri Zadorojnii. In his view, economic uncertainties, geopolitical shifts and structural change will shape the coming years, and their impact can only be predicted to a limited extent. „From a position of strength, we are positioning AUTODOC today to remain capable of acting effectively even under more challenging conditions.“ The first half of 2026 was marked by further development in AUTODOC’s European distribution and logistics network. The company’s warehouse in Belgium is fully operational and supports faster deliveries across the Benelux region and France. In the second quarter, AUTODOC also brought its new UK warehouse site online. It’s the second 3PL warehouse after BE15 in Belgium. „The opening of our Manchester facility marks an important step in our evolution from a global webshop to a local powerhouse”, says Zadorojnii. „Equally central to this development is the ongoing automation of our C27 site in Cheb, Czech Republic — a project that is progressing according to plan and will strengthen our logistics network when fully operational from 2027. Local presence and automated infrastructure together enable us to serve customers more directly and build long-term operational resilience.” Digital model for AUTODOC PRO AUTODOC also continued the digital evolution of its B2B business during the first half of 2026 while focusing on the path to profitable growth. The company is transitioning AUTODOC PRO towards a digital model in most countries by streamlining the operations, such as the returns process, and moving B2B interactions mainly to the high-performance online platform. As a result, the Group will focus even more on operational efficiency and find the strategic balance between growth and profitability. AUTODOC made the procurement process faster, more scalable and significantly more efficient for professional garages. This digital transition ensures that independent repair shops across Europe can access the dedicated catalogue and competitive pricing seamlessly, allowing AUTODOC to serve this vital segment with agility. Double-digit growth in sales and earnings The business development reflects, among other factors, strategic measures taken in the past. Sales revenue climbed by 12.8% year-on-year to €1,003.4 million (H1 2025: €889.6 million) in the first half of the year. Of this, €921.8 million (H1 2025: €825.4 million/11.7%) was attributable to the B2C segment and €81.6 million (H1 2025: €64.2 million/27.0%) to the B2B segment in the first six months of this year. „Our B2C business remains the heart and engine of our company. Even though the pace of growth has eased slightly, we are confident that the measures taken will support future growth and profitability“, says Lennart Schmidt, Chief Financial Officer of Autodoc SE. Gross profit increased by 11.8% to €422.9 million (H1 2025: €378.1 million). Adjusted EBITDA rose by 13.7% to €91.9 million (H1 2025: €80.9 million). At the EBITDA level, resulted in an adjusted EBITDA margin of 9.2% (H1 2025: 9.1%). „The first six months of 2026 underline the resiliency of our company yet highlight the need for proactive measures to maintain our market leadership. With the launch of our Marketplace in Poland and the scaling-up of our new UK warehouse, we are laying the groundwork for future growth. These steps will put us in a better position and enable us to strike a healthy balance between financial stability and strategic expansion“, says Schmidt. This is reflected among other things in the development of liquidity. Free cash flow amounted to €115.0 million (H1 2025: €82.7 million) in the first half year, which allowed for a dividend payout of €70.6 million (H1 2025: €59.5 million) in the second quarter 2026. Nevertheless, the cash balance rose to €182.5 million at the end of June (30.06.2025: €136.2 million). „Our robust free cash flow puts us in a position to finance all of our strategic initiatives from our own resources“, says Lennart Schmidt. More orders, more active customers and higher order values The number of orders rose from 9.4 million (H1 2025) to 10.2 million in the first half of 2026. AUTODOC also measures its economic success by the development of the number of active customers. Over the twelve-month period ended 30 June 2026, customers placed 19.8 million orders, compared with 17.9 million in the previous 12-month period. For the last twelve months as of 30 June 2026, the number of active customers was 9.7 million. This represents an increase of 0.9 million compared with the first half-year 2025. Average order value rose from €94.4 in the last twelve months as of 30 June 2025 to €97.2 in the same period 2026. Outlook for 2026 specified and confirmed In a challenging macroeconomic environment with geopolitical volatility, AUTODOC continues to expect sales revenue growth in the lower half of the range of 11% to 16% due to the strategic decision to move the B2B business to a mainly digital operating model, with growth supported by the consistent implementation of optimised customer acquisition measures as well as to a lower extent the further expansion of the MARKETPLACE model across European markets. „Due to a relentless focus on operational efficiency and a balanced approach between sustained growth and increasing profitability, we continue to expect an Adjusted EBITDA between €170.0 million and €195.0 million,“ says Schmidt. The number of orders is expected to increase in the high single-digit percentage range, facilitated by the continued expansion of the logistics infrastructure, including the full operational go-live of the Manchester warehouse in the United Kingdom in the second quarter. Schmidt: „We remain committed to our vision of being the leading European tech ecosystem connecting the automotive aftermarket, leveraging our AI capabilities to foster data-driven decisions and enhance the digital customer experience.“ Financial highlights 6M 2025 6M 2026 % Sales revenue 889.6 1,003.4 12.8% Gross profit 378.1 422.9 11.8% Adjusted EBITDA 80.9 91.9 13.7% Adjusted EBITDA margin 9.1% 9.2% 0.1%pp Net profit 24.4 48.0 97.0% Free cashflow 82.7 115.0 39.1% Cash and cash equivalents 136.2 182.5 34.0% Q2 2025 Q2 2026 % Sales revenue 462.3 518.5 12.2% Gross profit 199.0 218.5 9.8% Adjusted EBITDA 46.9 52.5 11.9% Adjusted EBITDA margin 10.2% 10.1% 0.0%pp Net profit 13.5 25.8 91.7% About AUTODOC AUTODOC is the leading digital pure-play automotive parts platform in Europe. The business, which was founded in Berlin in 2008 by Alexej Erdle, Max Wegner and Vitalij Kungel, has developed into one of the most exciting E-Commerce companies in Europe in a remarkably short period. Since November 2022, the Company has been operating as the European corporation Autodoc SE. The Management Board consists of Dmitri Zadorojnii (CEO) and Lennart Schmidt (CFO). As of 31 December 2025, AUTODOC’s product assortment comprises around 7.8 million SKUs from around 2,700 brand manufacturers – including car, truck and motorcycle parts, tires as well as adjacent products such as tools, accessories, oils, liquids and consumables – and has significantly increased over time. In 2025, AUTODOC generated sales revenue of €1.8 billion (2024: €1.6 billion). AUTODOC has online shops in 27 European countries and employs more than 5,500 people in 13 locations: Belgium, Czech Republic, France, Germany, Italy, Kazakhstan, Luxembourg, Moldova, the Netherlands, Poland, Portugal, Ukraine and the United Kingdom. Photograph: Ombudsman Republik Indonesia/Facebook Indonesia Double beds, aircon and big-screen TVs: Indonesia suspends officials over luxury prison cells Indonesia’s prisons have long faced allegations that well-connected inmates can obtain preferential treatment through bribery Associated Press Wed 30 Sep 2026 01.27 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Five Indonesian prison officials have been suspended after investigators found an apartment-style compound complete with airconditioners, big-screen televisions and expensive cars allegedly used by inmates at a prison near Jakarta. “We found strong indications that certain prisoners had access to special facilities unavailable to ordinary prisoners,” said Syafrida Rachmawati Rasahan, a member of Indonesia’s ombudsman, on Tuesday. “We encountered prisoners inside the residential compound and discovered facilities resembling home stays, apartments and villas rather than prison housing.” View image in fullscreen Indonesia’s ombudsman discovered facilities resembling home stays rather than prison cells. Photograph: Ombudsman Republik Indonesia/Facebook Investigators also reported finding sofas and dining areas in the units, and a gym and golf simulator under construction in the complex. The incident has drawn widespread public attention and renewed scrutiny of Indonesia’s prisons, which have long faced allegations that wealthy or well-connected prisoners can obtain preferential treatment through bribery. The allegations centre on Cibinong prison in Bogor, near Jakarta, where investigators from the ombudsman found more than 10 residential units separate from regular prison cells during a surprise inspection on 23 September, Rasahan said. Rudi Setiawan, inspector general of the ministry of immigration and corrections, said dozens of prisoners and prison employees had been questioned as part of the inquiry. “We have suspended five structural officials, including the Cibinong prison chief, who are suspected of being responsible for the incident uncovered by the ombudsman,” Setiawan said. The four-hectare (10-acre) Cibinong prison houses a mix of prisoners, including those convicted of corruption and other high-profile prisoners. The identities of prisoners allegedly living in the compound have not been officially disclosed. View image in fullscreen Dozens of prisoners and prison employees have been questioned as part of the inquiry. Photograph: Ombudsman Republik Indonesia/Facebook Lawmakers, anti-corruption activists and watchdog groups have urged authorities to identify which prisoners occupied the facilities and whether prison officials accepted payments in exchange for the privileges. The buildings were originally intended as official housing for prison personnel, but investigators are examining whether they were converted into unauthorised accommodation for prisoners, said Setiawan. The case is the latest embarrassment for the corrections system in Indonesia, which has struggled for years with overcrowding, corruption and repeated allegations that affluent prisoners can buy privileges unavailable to the broader prison population. Photograph: Reuters Pakistan Pakistan school roof collapse kills at least 34 children and teacher Another three pupils from al-Khair school in Peshawar in critical condition after search for survivors Reuters in Islamabad Thu 15 Oct 2026 04.25 EDT Last modified on Thu 15 Oct 2026 14.00 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google At least 34 schoolchildren and a female teacher have died after the roof of a school collapsed during morning classes in the northern Pakistani city ⁠of Peshawar. As panicked parents ​and relatives thronged the site of the privately run al-Khair school to search for their loved ones, rescue workers spent hours pulling children from the rubble. Most of the victims were under 13 years old ⁠and from low-income households. At least 45 children suffered injuries, ranging from minor wounds to severe trauma, said Arif Khattak, the regional director of emergency services. Map showing location of school and Lady Reading hospital in Peshawar Television footage showed rescuers clawing through debris with their bare hands and carrying bloodied children to ⁠waiting ambulances as people crowded the alley where the school stood. The roof of a higher floor collapsed on to classrooms below, crumpling two ​storeys of the building, a rescue official said. “The fatalities include ‌12 girl students and a female teacher,” said the Lady ‌Reading hospital spokesperson, Mohammad Asim. Three children remained in critical condition with head injuries, while most of the injured taken to the hospital ‌had been treated and discharged, he added. The incident took place at 8.48am local time (0348 GMT) and the rescue operation lasted for four to five hours, Khattak said. “It was a weak building structure,” said the Peshawar police chief, Mian Saeed. “Its roof was overloaded with construction on a weak structure, which caused the collapse.” Saeed said the school’s owner had been arrested and an investigation launched. A total of 110 students were attending lessons in three classrooms when the roof caved in. View image in fullscreen Mourners attend funeral prayers for children who died in the roof collapse. Photograph: Maaz Awan/AP Distraught relatives accused the school of ignoring concerns about ‌the building’s condition and demanded accountability. “Make an example of them, a lesson for all, so that no one dares open a school just to make money without providing facilities,” said Mohammad Zaman, who lost two nephews in the collapse. The ​school was located in a poor, crowded neighbourhood of Peshawar, the capital of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province, where Pakistan’s president imposed a state of emergency on Sunday, saying the provincial government had failed to tackle Islamist militancy from neighbouring Afghanistan, an allegation it denied. Pakistan spends less than 1% of its approximately $450bn (£340bn) GDP on education, leaving many families dependent on low-cost private schools. Many of those schools operate from poorly maintained rented buildings with limited oversight, contributing to recurring safety concerns. In June, at least ⁠14 children died when the roof of a tutoring centre housed in a dilapidated building collapsed in the ​eastern city of Lahore. There was no immediate comment ​from school officials. The country’s prime minister, Shehbaz Sharif, expressed ​sorrow over the tragedy and offered condolences to the victims’ families, his office said. Jawad Ahmad, whose son and daughter survived the incident, said the ‌news had left him devastated. “It felt ​as if someone had shot ​me in the chest when I learned that the school building had collapsed,” he said. The province, governed for years by the party of the jailed former prime minister Imran Khan, has frequently been at odds with the federal administration. Pakistan’s president, Asif Ali Zardari, imposed a new governor on the province when he declared the state of emergency on Sunday, sharpening the tensions. Photograph: Tolga Akmen/EPA Wildfires Burnham to reveal plans for AI unit to tackle wildfires after scorching summer PM will also announce funding for specialised protective gear and the deployment of military aircraft Pippa Neill Environment reporter Thu 22 Oct 2026 17.30 EDT Last modified on Thu 22 Oct 2026 17.31 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google The UK government is to create an AI Cobra unit to spot wildfires after this year’s record-breaking summer saw devastating blazes across the country. The country experienced its hottest-ever summer this year, with prolonged dry periods and extreme heat fuelling wildfires that triggered an emergency alert to mobile phones in England and Wales. Figures released on 8 October showed a clear upward trend in the number of fires recorded each year. The Met Office found that the climate crisis made this extreme heat about 130 times more likely. ‘It’s due to climate’: the people of Stourbridge on the town’s wildfires Read more At the government’s first wildfire resilience summit on Friday, Andy Burnham will announce plans for a new wildfire AI unit in the National Situation Centre, which is part of the Cobra briefing rooms. Businesses including Google, Airbus and VodafoneThree are expected to attend the summit to set out how satellite monitoring and early warning systems can help fight fires. The government said its new AI unit would enable it to “spot and fight fires faster”. The prime minister will also announce £45m for fire crews to buy wildfire-specific personal protective equipment (PPE). This comes after the Guardian revealed that more than half of the 29 fire services that responded to requests for information had no wildfire PPE. They included the Suffolk fire and rescue service, which had to deal with an “apocalyptic” wildfire earlier this summer that burned close to the Sizewell B nuclear power station and destroyed vast areas of a protected nature reserve . Standard particle-filtering respirators do not protect against dangerous gases such as carbon monoxide, which are heavily present in wildfire smoke. Standard PPE can also be too hot and heavy for wildfire conditions. This can cause crews to overheat, or remove their PPE altogether, exposing them to greater danger from heat, smoke and radiation. Firefighters voice growing concerns over water supplies to tackle UK wildfires Read more The prime minister will also announce that military planes and helicopters will be made available to fight wildfires on remote moorland, steep hillsides and other hard-to-reach terrain. The defence secretary, Wes Streeting , said: “As the threat of wildfires in the UK grows, defence will step up to provide greater support to our emergency services and protect military training areas across the country.” The government will also look at tougher local restrictions or product bans to stop people starting fires when the risk is high. In August, Burnham announced a temporary ban on sales of disposable barbecues. He has also been criticised for failing to address the climate emergency in his wildfire response. Farmers will also be given funding to make landscapes more resilient to fires. This announcement comes after the government quietly scrapped plans announced under the Conservative government to prepare the countryside in England for wildfires. This revelation led Alistair Carmichael, a Scottish Liberal Democrat MP and chair of the Commons environment, food and rural affairs committee, to raise “serious questions about whether this summer’s wildfires could have looked different with more resources on the ground”. The government also said it would allocate £25m to restore dried-out peatlands in England so they hold more water and act as natural firebreaks, as well as provide financial support for farmers to fireproof their land. Rewilded land remains green amid drought-stricken English countryside, images show Read more This new grant scheme is expected to run from April 2027 to April 2029. Environmental campaigner and author Guy Shrubsole said: “For decades, wealthy grouse moor owners have drained our peat bogs, turning them into a tinderbox. This grant will help reverse that destruction, but must be followed by a new round of landscape recovery funding, and duties on landowners to repair the damage done. It’s time to make England wet again.” The prime minister said: “I stood in Stourbridge and watched families lose everything. I will never forget it. Our firefighters were heroes that day, but heroes shouldn’t have to fight with one hand tied behind their backs. “Crews will now have the kit they need to stay safe and military aircraft will stand ready to help tackle wildfires from the sky. We cannot put people through another summer like this one.” Explore more on these topics Wildfires Climate crisis Google Airbus Vodafone Andy Burnham Wes Streeting news Share Reuse this content Most viewed Most viewed US news US politics Midterms 2026 World Climate crisis Middle East Ukraine US immigration Soccer Business Environment Tech Science Newsletters The Filter Wellness
